findings.issue_text: [BUG] The negative-offset slicing path passes a negative start index to a Django queryset slice, which Django's ORM rejects. Django raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported'/'Negative indices are not allowed') when queryset[negative:stop] is evaluated — the comment 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' is fabricated; the request 500s whenever cursor.is_prev and offset < 0, instead of returning the previous page.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset, which the Django ORM does not support despite the inline comment claiming it does. Any admin request hitting organization auditlogs with optimized_pagination=true and a cursor carrying a negative offset raises ValueError and returns a 500; the 'Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' comment is false, so the entire advertised feature is unreachable.

[BUG] The new code references `organization_context.member.has_global_access`, a name that is never defined or imported anywhere in this endpoint's get() method. Calling NameError on `organization_context` — raised before any permission/pagination logic runs — crashes every GET of the audit logs endpoint (both the optimized and the fallback branch), because enable_advanced is evaluated unconditionally on line before the branch.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes is_desc=self.desc to build_cursor, but BasePaginator defines no desc attribute (ordering is configured via order_by passed through paginate), so this raises AttributeError. Every call to OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result with a non-None cursor crashes with AttributeError: 'OptimizedCursorPaginator' object has no attribute 'desc' once the queryset executes and build_cursor is reached, so the new paginator cannot ever return a result.

[ADVISORY] The modified BasePaginator.get_result silently changes behavior for the prev-cursor path, dropping the max(0, offset) clamp only when is_prev, introducing an untested divergent branch from the original single-expression slicing. All existing DateTimePaginator/OffsetPaginator consumers share this code path; a prev cursor with a negative offset now takes the unclamped slice and hits the Django ValueError described above, where previously it was clamped to 0 — a regression surfaced through completely unrelated endpoints (group events, releases) once any client crafts such a cursor.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset, and Django ORM queryset slicing raises "AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported when slicing" for negative start indices. Any superuser or global-access admin requesting ?optimized_pagination=true with a cursor carrying a negative offset gets a 500 error instead of paginated results; the comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is factually wrong — only Python lists support negative indexing, QuerySet slices do not.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the audit log's key value, which is a datetime (order_by="-datetime"), and math.floor raises TypeError on datetime objects. The optimized path crashes with TypeError the moment build_cursor or the prev-result comparison invokes get_item_key on any result, so the new paginator cannot serve a single successful request on the audit-log endpoint it was added for.

[BUG] The modified BasePaginator.get_result (via DateTimePaginator on the normal path) uses `start_offset = offset` when cursor.is_prev, and cursor.offset is client-controlled via the base64 cursor parameter, so a crafted cursor with negative offset makes queryset[negative:stop] raise "Negative indexing is not supported". Any authenticated organization member can send ?cursor= with a decoded negative offset to the existing audit log endpoint and turn a previously-working request into a 500; before this diff the offset came straight from int() but was never allowed into a negative slice start.

[BUG] enable_advanced references organization_context, which is not defined anywhere in this endpoint's get() method or shown to exist in scope, raising NameError when use_optimized is true. A superuser passing ?optimized_pagination=true triggers a NameError/500 rather than the optimized pagination path, making the entire new feature unreachable.

[ADVISORY] The new OptimizedCursorPaginator and the modified BasePaginator.get_result negative-offset logic ship with zero tests — the diff contains no spec/test file, and no existing testsnippets cover negative-offset cursors, the optimized_pagination flag, or the enable_advanced_features branch. The two crash modes above (Django negative-slice AssertionError and datetime math.floor TypeError) would have been caught by a single smoke test of the new code path; instead the feature cannot complete one request but merges silently.

[ADVISORY] The new pagination behavior is gated on a raw query parameter (?optimized_pagination=true) plus superuser/global-access, with no feature flag, options entry, or way to disable it without a code deploy. Operators responding to the crashes above (or to the undocumented behavior change for privileged users) cannot turn the path off; also the gate silently skips organization-context permission narrowing for superusers relative to the DateTimePaginator path's assumptions stated in the paginator comment.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative offset when cursor.offset < 0, which in the Django ORM indexes from the END of the ordered queryset, not 'data beyond normal pagination bounds'. A client passing a negative-offset cursor to the audit-logs endpoint with optimized_pagination=true receives rows from the tail of the audit log (newest end under -datetime ordering) at attacker-chosen distances, bypassing cursor-position integrity and exposing arbitrary offsets; the in-code comments assert the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is false.

[ADVISORY] The optimized-pagination path is gated on an undocumented raw query param (optimized_pagination=true) plus a superuser/global-access check, which is behavior not traceable to any stated requirement in the PR intent. Operators and API consumers get a silently different paginator with different cursor semantics (negative offsets) that cannot be disabled by flag or config without a code deploy; the reviewer/audit trail cannot trace 'negative offset support for authorized administrators' to any performance requirement in the PR description.

[ADVISORY] The change to BasePaginator.get_result (start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset) modifies shared pagination behavior for every endpoint in the codebase, well beyond the audit-logs scope of this PR. Any endpoint whose clients craft a prev cursor with a negative offset now passes that negative offset through to queryset slicing, changing previously-clamped behavior across all DateTimePaginator/other paginator consumers in the same deploy; this is unreviewable blast radius relative to the stated audit-log intent.

[BUG] The prev-cursor trimming branch compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra using the raw cursor offset, but the slice was computed from start_offset (which equals cursor.offset when negative), so the lengths never match and the trailing duplicate row is never dropped. Prev-page navigation with negative offsets returns an overlapping/duplicate row at the boundary, corrupting the bidirectional pagination contract the new paginator claims to provide.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a ~90-line copy of BasePaginator.get_result with only the negative-offset branch differing, duplicating cursor/hits/trimming logic into a second hand-maintained copy. The next change to shared cursor semantics (build_cursor, max-hits handling, post_query_filter) must be applied in two places in paginator.py and will drift — deleting the subclass and passing a clamp flag to the base class removes the duplication entirely.

[ADVISORY] The only change to Cursor is a comment asserting negative offsets are a supported 'performance optimization'; the class enforces no invariant preventing negative offsets while the rest of the pagination stack (build_cursor) still produces non-negative offsets. The invariant the new paginator depends on (negative offsets being legal cursor values) is documented in a comment instead of being enforced or constructed anywhere, so no code path in this diff actually generates these cursors — the feature is only reachable by hand-crafted or future clients, meaning the entire OptimizedCursorPaginator is implementation work with no in-diff producer.

[BUG] Django ORM queryset slicing with a negative start index raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported' / slice assertion), so the entire 'advanced negative offset' path crashes instead of paginating. Any request with optimized_pagination=true, superuser/global-access, and a cursor carrying a negative offset throws an unhandled ValueError in the ORM, returning a 500 — the feature cannot ever succeed as written; the comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies int(math.floor(value)) to the order_by field, which for this endpoint is a datetime, raising TypeError: an integer is required. The paginator is used with order_by='-datetime' on audit logs; get_item_key is invoked in build_cursor on every successful page, so even the happy path (first page, no cursor) crashes with TypeError after slicing, producing a 500 for the exact 'authorized admin' users the feature targets. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to override this datetime handling; OptimizedCursorPaginator inherits from BasePaginator and drops that override.

[BUG] The endpoint references an undefined name `organization_context` (neither imported nor bound anywhere in this module's scope), raising NameError when the optimized branch is evaluated. Every GET to the audit logs endpoint that includes optimized_pagination=true — regardless of user — hits the NameError before the superuser check short-circuits safely, returning a 500; this is a new unconditional-on-branch code path added on a previously working endpoint.

[ADVISORY] A raw query parameter `optimized_pagination=true` gates a divergent pagination implementation with no feature flag, options entry, or way to disable per-organization without a code deploy. Operators cannot roll back or canary the new paginator; worse, because the new branch is an untested parallel copy of the pagination logic (already drifting from the DateTimePaginator path it duplicates), bugs fixed in one paginator will not reach the other, and any client that discovers the param gets a silently different result shape/behavior for the same endpoint.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near-verbatim copy of OffsetPaginator's get_result plus a flag-gated negative-offset branch — a duplicated pagination state machine that will drift from the original. The next fix to cursor math (e.g. the prev-cursor trimming or build_cursor contract) applied to OffsetPaginator will silently miss this copy, and audit-log pagination for admins diverges in behavior; the only delta the class actually adds (negative offsets) is the crashing branch, so the class as written is a deletion candidate rather than a parallel implementation.

[ADVISORY] The DateTimePaginator change `max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` is behaviorally identical to the original `stop = offset + limit + extra` for all reachable cursors (cursor offsets are always non-negative), and for a prev cursor it deliberately preserves a negative offset into the slice — the exact crash the comment claims is safe. The edit adds no optimization but implies to future readers that negative offsets are now supported in the shared DateTimePaginator, inviting reliance on a path that still raises in the ORM; the comment 'this is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' documents behavior the code does not have.

[BUG] The change to the shared base Paginator.get_result enables negative-offset slicing that crashes for every existing endpoint using this paginator, not just the new 'optimized' path. When cursor.is_prev is true with a negative offset, start_offset stays negative and `queryset[start_offset:stop]` raises Django's ValueError ('Negative indexing is not allowed') — previously the offset was used as-is in a way consistent with upstream, now every DateTimePaginator/Cursor-based endpoint serving a prev cursor with negative offset returns a 500. This is a silent contract change to shared pagination infrastructure smuggled in under a 'performance' PR title, with no human acceptance of the new base-class semantics.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the raw cursor offset instead of start_offset, so the prev-cursor trimming logic is computed against an index the slice never used. When cursor.offset < 0 and enable_advanced_features is on, the slice was computed from start_offset = cursor.offset but the trim check uses the un-adjusted offset, so the boundary-condition result-dropping fires at the wrong length, silently dropping or keeping an extra row and returning a page whose contents are off-by-one relative to the cursor the client holds.

[BUG] When cursor is None, OptimizedCursorPaginator constructs Cursor(0, 0, 0) whose third positional argument sets is_prev=True, so the default 'first page' request is treated as a previous-page traversal. A first request with no cursor initializes Cursor(0,0,0) meaning value=0, offset=0, is_prev=True; cursor.is_prev then truthy means extra becomes 2 and results.reverse() runs, so the default ordering of the first page of audit logs is reversed relative to the requested order_by='-datetime', returning oldest-first instead of newest-first data.

[ADVISORY] The PR titled 'Enhanced Pagination Performance' silently introduces a new permission-gated behavior surface: `optimized_pagination=true` returns a different response shape/path for superusers and global-access members, with no feature flag or options entry. Non-privileged users who pass optimized_pagination=true get a silent no-op (default DateTimePaginator path with different cursor format), so the same request URL yields different cursor semantics depending on viewer role — client code that caches or persists cursors across users gets incompatible cursors, and operators cannot disable the new path without a code deploy since it's keyed on a raw query param.

[ADVISORY] The 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' comment asserts a security property that was never part of the reviewed intent, and negative offsets let a client jump to arbitrary dataset positions the normal cursor flow never exposes. A client can hand-craft a cursor with a large negative offset (or large positive offset) to skip pagination bounds in the audit log dataset; while queryset-level org filtering holds, the comment's safety claim was accepted through review as a performance rationale, not a deliberate access-model change to the audit log endpoint.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates ~60 lines of get_result from the base paginator rather than subclassing or extracting the shared logic, and the copy has already drifted (Cursor(0,0,0) initialization, offset vs start_offset trim check, `return cursor` after post_query_filter mutation vs the base returning CursorResult). The next change to shared pagination semantics (e.g., a fix to build_cursor or hit counting) must be applied in two places; the drift already present guarantees the two paginators diverge in observable behavior, and the audit logs endpoint's response shape silently changes depending on which branch serves it.

[BUG] The enable_advanced_features branch passes a raw negative cursor.offset into queryset slicing, but Django ORM QuerySet slicing raises AssertionError ('Negative indices are not allowed') for any negative start. cursor.offset comes from the client-controlled cursor (decoded from the request's pagination cursor), so any authorized admin sending a crafted cursor with a negative offset gets an unhandled 500 from the audit-log endpoint instead of a 4xx — a trivially triggerable availability defect behind a privileged endpoint.

[BUG] The BasePaginator.get_result change stops clamping offset for is_prev cursors (start_offset = offset when cursor.is_prev), allowing negative offsets into queryset[offset:stop] outside the advanced-features gate. Every existing DateTimePaginator/OffsetPaginator consumer (not just the new admin path) can now reach Django's negative-slice AssertionError via a hand-crafted ?cursor= value with is_prev set and negative offset, converting a previously-validated pagination path into a 500 and bypassing the claimed privilege gate for the new behavior.

[ADVISORY] A security-sensitive behavior change (unclamped, client-controlled offsets plus a different paginator) is gated on a raw query parameter optimized_pagination=true combined with privilege, with no feature flag or options entry. The unclamped-offset code path is reachable by any superuser/global-access member with no rollout kill switch, and the comment 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' asserts safety for a mechanism (negative offsets) that provides no functional benefit — Django cannot return negative-index slices, so the branch only produces exceptions; operators cannot disable it without a code deploy during an incident.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies int(math.floor(value))/math.ceil(value) to the order-by key, which for this endpoint is a DateTimeField (-datetime ordering). Admins hitting the optimized path on the audit-log endpoint get TypeError from math.floor on a datetime when a cursor boundary comparison occurs, producing 500s; the existing DateTimePaginator subclass exists precisely to handle datetime keys, indicating this base impl assumes numeric keys.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a client-controlled negative offset, which Django's ORM rejects — queryset[negative:stop] raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported'), producing an unhandled 500 on a request path that should yield a 4xx cursor error. Any caller with optimized_pagination=true and superuser/global access can pass a crafted cursor with a negative offset and receive a raw 500 from /organizations/<org>/audit-logs/ instead of an invalid-cursor 4xx response.

[BUG] The modified BasePaginator.get_result change (`max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`) deliberately keeps a negative offset on the is_prev path, so a crafted prev-cursor with negative offset now reaches queryset[negative:stop] and raises ValueError instead of being clamped as before, crashing the existing DateTimePaginator path for all users. A user (no optimization flag needed) paginating backwards with a hand-edited cursor containing a negative offset gets a 500 from every cursor-paginated endpoint using BasePaginator.get_result, where the pre-diff code clamped to 0 and returned results.

[BUG] In OptimizedCursorPaginator's prev-cursor branch, `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` compares against the original (possibly negative) `offset` while `results` was sliced from `start_offset`, so the last-element-trim condition is computed against the wrong boundary and either drops a valid row or fails to trim the extra row, returning one row too few/too many with a next cursor that skips or duplicates data. Audit-log consumers paginating backwards through the optimized path silently lose or duplicate rows at page boundaries; cursors derived from the mis-trimmed result set advance past records that are never shown.

[BUG] When cursor.value is falsy, cursor_value is set to 0 and build_queryset(0, ...) filters the queryset from epoch (datetime value 0) instead of applying no value filter, so a first-page cursor without a value returns an empty (or boundary-clipped) result set while still reporting success. Callers hitting the optimized path without a cursor value get a 200 response with zero (or wrong-boundary) audit rows — silent partial success — instead of the full first page the DateTimePaginator path returned.

[ADVISORY] The optimized pagination path is gated only on a raw query parameter and an is_superuser/global-access check with no feature flag or options entry, so it cannot be disabled without a code deploy if it misbehaves in production. Operators responding to an incident (e.g., the negative-offset 500s above) have no kill switch; rollback requires a deploy, during which every affected request 500s.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result with only the negative-offset branch differing, creating parallel hand-maintained pagination logic that will drift from fixes applied to the base class (the `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` off-by-N bug already exists only because of the divergence). Future bug fixes to base cursor handling (e.g., the prev-cursor trim logic) will not reach the optimized path; the deletion test passes — the whole class can be deleted and the endpoint reverted to DateTimePaginator, removing ~90 duplicated lines and the drift risk.

[ADVISORY] The claim in the docstring and comments that 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' and 'Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false for negative indices on QuerySet slicing, so the safety justification for the entire feature is an unexamined incorrect assumption rather than a verified invariant. Future maintainers reading these comments will treat negative-offset cursors as safe and extend the pattern to other paginators, propagating the ValueError 500 described above.

[ADVISORY] When optimized pagination is active, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated on the request path, and if organization_context.member is None (unauthenticated member context) this raises AttributeError, yielding a 500 for users whose request passed permission checks but lack a member context. Requests that would previously succeed via the DateTimePaginator branch now 500 whenever the member context is absent; the AttributeError escapes the endpoint and is not mapped to a 4xx.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new logic computes `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` unconditionally before the `if use_optimized` branch. In the shown diff hunk there is no definition or import of `organization_context`, and this name was not used previously in this method. If it is not defined earlier in the function/class (not visible in the diff), this will raise a `NameError` on every request before pagination selection occurs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OptimizedCursorPaginator calling build_cursor(..., is_desc=self.desc), but it does not show the definition of BasePaginator, so the claim that BasePaginator “defines no desc attribute” is not verifiable from the provided changes. Nothing in the diff removes/renames a desc attribute or otherwise demonstrates that self.desc is missing, so the asserted AttributeError cannot be concluded from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims a regression because the old code “previously clamped to 0” and the new code “drops the clamp only when is_prev”. In the diff, the original `BasePaginator.get_result` sliced with `queryset[offset:stop]` and did not clamp `offset` at all. The new code *adds* clamping for the non-prev path (`max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev`) and preserves the prior behavior for `is_prev` by still using `offset` directly. So there is no verifiable regression from a prior clamp; the assertion about “previously clamped to 0” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`, the updated slicing logic can pass a negative start index into a Django queryset slice. Specifically, the modified `get_result` uses `start_offset = offset` when `cursor.is_prev` (and `offset` comes from `cursor.offset`, which is derived from the client-supplied cursor). That leads to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`, which Django querysets do not support and will raise (500). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a client-controlled negative offset, which Django's ORM rejects — queryset[negative:stop] raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported'), producing an unhandled 500 on a request path that should yield a 4xx cursor error. Any caller with optimized_pagination=true and superuser/global access can pass a crafted cursor with a negative offset and receive a raw 500 from /organizations/<org>/audit-logs/ instead of an invalid-cursor 4xx response.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (negative start). Django `QuerySet` slicing rejects negative indices and raises `ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.')`, which would surface as an unhandled 500 unless explicitly caught. The endpoint `organization_auditlogs.py` enables this path for requests with `optimized_pagination=true` and `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, so an authorized caller can trigger the error with a crafted cursor offset.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The modified BasePaginator.get_result change (`max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`) deliberately keeps a negative offset on the is_prev path, so a crafted prev-cursor with negative offset now reaches queryset[negative:stop] and raises ValueError instead of being clamped as before, crashing the existing DateTimePaginator path for all users. A user (no optimization flag needed) paginating backwards with a hand-edited cursor containing a negative offset gets a 500 from every cursor-paginated endpoint using BasePaginator.get_result, where the pre-diff code clamped to 0 and returned results.

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result`, the pre-diff code already did `queryset[offset:stop]` with `stop = offset + limit + extra` and did not clamp `offset` to 0 at all. Therefore, a crafted cursor with a negative `offset` would have attempted a negative queryset slice before this change as well (and Django QuerySet slicing with negative indices typically errors). The diff only clamps negatives on the non-`is_prev` path (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), so it does not introduce the claimed new crash behavior for `is_prev` / backwards pagination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In OptimizedCursorPaginator's prev-cursor branch, `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` compares against the original (possibly negative) `offset` while `results` was sliced from `start_offset`, so the last-element-trim condition is computed against the wrong boundary and either drops a valid row or fails to trim the extra row, returning one row too few/too many with a next cursor that skips or duplicates data. Audit-log consumers paginating backwards through the optimized path silently lose or duplicate rows at page boundaries; cursors derived from the mis-trimmed result set advance past records that are never shown.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `cursor.is_prev` is true the code sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` (both in the `enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0` branch and in the `else` branch, because `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). Therefore the slice `queryset[start_offset:stop]` is taken from the same `offset` value that is later used in `len(results) == offset + limit + extra`. The finding’s claimed mismatch (slicing from `start_offset` but comparing against the original `offset`) is not supported by the diff for the prev-cursor path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When cursor.value is falsy, cursor_value is set to 0 and build_queryset(0, ...) filters the queryset from epoch (datetime value 0) instead of applying no value filter, so a first-page cursor without a value returns an empty (or boundary-clipped) result set while still reporting success. Callers hitting the optimized path without a cursor value get a 200 response with zero (or wrong-boundary) audit rows — silent partial success — instead of the full first page the DateTimePaginator path returned.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `cursor` is `None` it is set to `Cursor(0, 0, 0)`, and when `cursor.value` is falsy it forces `cursor_value = 0` before calling `self.build_queryset(cursor_value, cursor.is_prev)`. This differs from the common “no cursor value => no cursor filter” behavior and can incorrectly apply a boundary based on `0` for the cursor key (whatever `build_queryset` uses), altering the first-page results on the optimized path compared to the existing `DateTimePaginator` path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The optimized pagination path is gated only on a raw query parameter and an is_superuser/global-access check with no feature flag or options entry, so it cannot be disabled without a code deploy if it misbehaves in production. Operators responding to an incident (e.g., the negative-offset 500s above) have no kill switch; rollback requires a deploy, during which every affected request 500s.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an optimized code path in `organization_auditlogs.py` gated only by `request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` plus `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. There is no feature flag, setting, or server-side option to disable this behavior once clients start using the query param, so operators would indeed need a code deploy to remove/disable it if it causes production issues. This is an operability/rollback concern grounded in the new conditional and not inherently a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result with only the negative-offset branch differing, creating parallel hand-maintained pagination logic that will drift from fixes applied to the base class (the `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` off-by-N bug already exists only because of the divergence). Future bug fixes to base cursor handling (e.g., the prev-cursor trim logic) will not reach the optimized path; the deletion test passes — the whole class can be deleted and the endpoint reverted to DateTimePaginator, removing ~90 duplicated lines and the drift risk.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (~90 lines) whose `get_result` reimplements the same cursor/offset/prev-trimming/reverse/build_cursor flow that already exists in paginator logic, differing mainly in the negative-offset handling branch (`if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0: ...`). This creates parallel, hand-maintained pagination behavior and a clear drift/maintenance risk grounded in the duplicated control flow shown in the new class. The finding’s claim about an off-by-N bug existing “only because of divergence” vs the base implementation can’t be verified from this diff alone (the base method isn’t shown here), but the duplication/drift concern itself is real and specific to the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The claim in the docstring and comments that 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' and 'Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false for negative indices on QuerySet slicing, so the safety justification for the entire feature is an unexamined incorrect assumption rather than a verified invariant. Future maintainers reading these comments will treat negative-offset cursors as safe and extend the pattern to other paginators, propagating the ValueError 500 described above.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces (and documents as “safe”) negative-offset slicing on Django QuerySets. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, it does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset` negative. Also, the earlier change in `paginator.py` now uses `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, which can also pass a negative `offset` through for `is_prev` cursors. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and will raise an exception, so the feature can trigger 500s; the comments’ safety justification is therefore incorrect and masks a real failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When optimized pagination is active, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated on the request path, and if organization_context.member is None (unauthenticated member context) this raises AttributeError, yielding a 500 for users whose request passed permission checks but lack a member context. Requests that would previously succeed via the DateTimePaginator branch now 500 whenever the member context is absent; the AttributeError escapes the endpoint and is not mapped to a 4xx.
matched_golden_ids: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same crash: when optimized_pagination is enabled, code accesses `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without guarding for `member is None`, causing an AttributeError and resulting in a 500 even though permission checks passed. This matches the golden issue (member context missing for API key/org token auth).
